docs.title: CleanWRT: OpenWrt for the Arcadyan AW1000
docs.text:
CleanWRT is an independent, community build of OpenWrt 25.12.5 for the Arcadyan AW1000 5G router (Qualcomm IPQ8072, Quectel RG500Q-EA modem). It adds AWvoice, which turns the RJ11 socket into a working phone line, a working 5G stack, a modern interface and a curated set of opt-in apps to stock OpenWrt. It is built in the open on GitHub from pinned sources.

If you own an AW1000 and want OpenWrt on it, with a desk phone on the RJ11 socket and a 5G link that reconnects on its own, this is the place to start. The pages below take you from "is my router supported?" to a flashed, working router, and tell you how to get out if something goes wrong.

Not affiliated with OpenWrt

CleanWRT is Powered by OpenWrt and is not affiliated with or endorsed by the OpenWrt project. OpenWrt® is a registered trademark of Software Freedom Conservancy (SFC).

  • Plug in a phone: AWvoice

    Use a normal desk phone on the router's RJ11 socket and make calls over your SIM. No extra box, no PBX, no SIP account.

    AWvoice

  • Install it

    Flash from the stock firmware (UART + TFTP) or from an existing OpenWrt install.

    Installation

  • Check the layout first

    The image needs the expanded flash layout. Flashing it on the stock layout can brick the router.

    MTD layout

  • Know the way back

    Failsafe, U-Boot, serial console. Read this before you flash, not after.

    Recovery

  • Use the 5G modem

    QModem, signal details, SMS, TTL, and what a modem firmware upgrade involves.

    The 5G modem

docs.title: What you get on top of stock OpenWrt
docs.text:
• AWvoice, phone calls on the RJ11 port: an ordinary desk phone makes and takes calls over the SIM, with caller id, call waiting, hold, a three-way join, recall of a held call, a call log, speed dial, call blocking and alarm calls. See AWvoice.
  • A 5G stack that works out of the box: QModem UI, auto-dial, dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 data, TTL control, SMS, a registration fix for data-only SIMs, per-interface vnStat accounting.
  • A modern interface: the Apex theme with dark and light mode, a sidebar, a mobile drawer and card-style status widgets.
  • Real front-panel LEDs: a small daemon that shows 5G type, signal quality and internet reachability, with a night mode. See Front-panel LEDs.
  • Proxy and VPN tools: Passwall, Passwall2, HomeProxy, WireGuard, OpenVPN, Tailscale and Cloudflare Tunnel, all installed and all off until you configure them.
  • Opt-in apps: file sharing, DLNA, printer server, Syncthing, AdGuard Home, qBittorrent, Adblock and more. Nothing listens on your network until you tick Enable.
  • Safe defaults: LuCI over HTTPS, BBR congestion control, no open services, no hidden remote access.
  • Verifiable releases: every release has checksums and a provenance bundle (the full build configuration, the pinned sources and the package manifest).

docs.title: Status
docs.text: CleanWRT is a release-candidate series (25.12.5-rc1). The image is built on GitHub Actions from the sources pinned in the repository. Read the known limits before relying on it for anything important.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
What is CleanWRT?

CleanWRT is an independent build of OpenWrt 25.12.5 for the Arcadyan AW1000 5G router. On top of stock OpenWrt it adds a working RJ11 phone port (AWvoice), a 5G modem stack that dials and recovers by itself, the Apex theme, front-panel LED management and a set of apps that stay off until you enable them.

Which routers does CleanWRT support?

Only the Arcadyan AW1000 (the Telstra variant) with the expanded flash layout. Never flash it on another router, because an image built for a different partition table can brick the device. See Hardware and MTD layout.

How is CleanWRT different from stock OpenWrt on the AW1000?

It is OpenWrt 25.12.5 with the AW1000 pieces already working: the phone port with VoLTE calls, QModem for the 5G modem, a modern dark and light interface, LEDs that show 5G type and signal quality, and VPN and proxy tools that are installed but off by default.

Is CleanWRT free to use?

Yes. The build configuration, patches and scripts are GPL-2.0-only. The bundled packages keep their own licences, and QModem adds a non-commercial clause, so read Licence and notices before any business use.

docs.title: AWvoice: an RJ11 phone port with VoLTE calls on the AW1000
docs.text:
AWvoice turns the AW1000's RJ11 socket into a working phone line. Plug an ordinary desk phone into the router and make and take calls over the SIM card, with no extra box, no PBX and no SIP account. It is the headline feature of CleanWRT, and it ships with the 25.12.5-rc1 release, in the same way QModem is the 5G modem app.

Pre-release documentation

This page describes the current state of AWvoice. Details, especially the setup steps, can change before 25.12.5-rc1 is published.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Calls incoming and outgoing calls with clear speech both ways Tones dial tone, ringing tone, busy and congestion tones In a call DTMF, caller id on the handset display (FSK, Bellcore or ETSI, or the DTMF variant, sent before or after the first ring), hook flash Call waiting a second call is announced during a call; hold it, swap between the two, or refuse it Three-way join join two calls into one conversation: hook flash, then 3 (can be switched off in Settings) Recall put the handset down with a call on hold and the phone rings back; lift it to take the call back Call log incoming, outgoing and missed calls, with the names from your phone book Phone book contacts with speed dial Call blocking by direction (incoming or outgoing), by number or by prefix Hotline dial a number automatically when the handset is lifted Calling-line restriction hide your number, and the network's service codes Phone LED solid while the line is ready, a fast blink while a call rings, a slow blink while the handset is off hook (the rates can be set) Alarm calls wake-up calls at a time you choose Line test check the line from the web page A web page Services → AWvoice(RJ11) with live status, calls, rules, settings, health and tests

docs.title: Hook flash codes
docs.text:
During a call, press the handset's flash (R) key, then one digit. These are the standard network codes:

After the flash press What happens 1 end the current call and take the other one (the waiting or the held call) 2 put the current call on hold and take the other one; with two calls it swaps them, and with one held call it takes that call back 0 refuse the waiting call, or release the held call 3 join the two calls into a three-way conversation (needs two calls, and three-way calling switched on in Settings)

Set the flash key's timing in Settings, if your handset's flash key is longer or shorter than the default.

docs.title: Recall
docs.text: If you hang up while a call is on hold, the call is not lost. The phone rings back until you lift the handset, which takes the call back, or the other side ends it.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The call itself is carried by the router's 5G modem (VoLTE), which AWvoice controls over its AT port. The router drives the line-interface chip of the RJ11 port and bridges the audio in the kernel, so the phone behaves like a normal one. No Asterisk, no SIP.

AWvoice has three parts: a kernel module for the line chip (GPL-2.0-only), the phone daemon, and the LuCI page.

A watchdog in the kernel puts the line chip back in reset whenever the phone service stops, so the line is never left ringing.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
Read this before you use it

  • About 46 V DC is present on the RJ11 contacts, and up to about 100 V while the phone is ringing. Do not touch the contacts.
  • Not for emergency use. The line works only while the router has power, the modem is registered for VoLTE and the operator carries the call. There is no emergency-call certification and no battery backup. Keep a mobile phone at hand for emergencies.
  • The block list never blocks your country's national emergency numbers, and a dialled emergency number is never replaced by a speed-dial entry.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A SIM and an operator that provide VoLTE (voice over LTE).
  • The modem in PCM slave mode. AWvoice warns in the log if it is not, and does not change it by itself.
  • Nothing else for the line chip: its board file ships with AWvoice and is installed on the first start.
  • An ordinary analogue phone with an RJ11 plug.

AWvoice reads the modem's audio mode and its VoLTE (IMS) state and shows them on the Health area of the page. It does not change them itself.

docs.title: Turn it on
docs.text:
AWvoice is installed with CleanWRT but the phone service starts only when you enable it, so the line is never left ringing by accident:

uci set awvoice.main.enabled=1
uci commit awvoice
/etc/init.d/awvoice start

The defaults fit the AW1000. The settings the page does not show (the modem's AT interface number, the LED name) are in /etc/config/awvoice.

docs.title: The web page
docs.text:
Services → AWvoice(RJ11) is one page for everything:

  • live status: the line (idle, off hook, ringing, in a call), the current call, the voice network and the signal;
  • calls: the call log, with names from the phone book;
  • phone book and speed dial;
  • rules: call blocking, forwarding and alarm calls;
  • settings: caller id mode, hook-flash timing, tones, audio levels, call waiting, hotline and the line LED;
  • health and tests: the AT port, the line, the modem, counters and the log, with ring, line and loopback tests.

docs.title: Frequently asked questions
docs.text:
How do I make phone calls on the Arcadyan AW1000?

Install CleanWRT, which includes AWvoice, plug an ordinary analogue desk phone into the RJ11 socket, enable the phone service and lift the handset. Calls go out over the router's 5G modem with your SIM's number.

Which phones work on the RJ11 port?

An ordinary analogue (tone dial) phone with an RJ11 plug. A handset with a display also shows the caller id.

Does AWvoice need Asterisk, SIP or a second phone number?

No. There is no PBX and no SIP account. The cellular network is the exchange and the SIM's number is the line's number.

Does the AW1000 need VoLTE for voice calls?

Yes. The call is carried by the modem over VoLTE, so you need a SIM and an operator that provide VoLTE. The modem must also be in PCM slave mode, which AWvoice checks and reports.

Can I use it for emergency calls?

No. The line works only while the router has power, the modem is registered for VoLTE and the operator carries the call, and there is no battery backup. Keep a mobile phone at hand.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Hide my number (CLIR) and call forwarding can be refused by the operator's network when the phone registers (+CME ERROR: 30). The page hides both while that is the case.
  • Giving up a second call while it still rings ends every call: the modem cannot release a ringing leg on its own.
  • The modem's IMS registration may not come up after a cold boot, rarely. The page then shows "Not registered", and a modem restart clears it.
  • Alarm calls trust the router's clock, which must be set. A wrong but plausible clock rings them at the wrong time.
  • Not for emergency calls, see the safety box.

docs.title: Source code
docs.text: AWvoice is developed in its own repository, Pr0Luci/openwrt-aw1000-voice-awvoice, which has the standard feed layout (see Build from source). All three parts are GPL-2.0-only; see Licence and notices.

docs.title: Build from source
docs.text: Anyone can rebuild a release. The repository holds only build configuration, patches and the rootfs overlay: no firmware binaries and no package source. Packages are fetched from their upstream feeds at build time, every one pinned to a commit.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text:
The firmware repository pins several smaller repositories, listed with their documentation on the Repositories page. This is the layout of the firmware repository itself:

Path What it is configs/arcadyan_aw1000.seed the package selection and image identity configs/local-packages.pin out-of-feed packages, pinned to a commit configs/license-overrides.tsv licences for packages that record none feeds.conf.default every feed, pinned to a commit feeds-src/cwfeed/ the vendored feed (qBittorrent stack, AdGuard Home app, Syncthing app) files/ the rootfs overlay (first-boot scripts, defaults, banner) patches/feeds/ patches applied to the pinned feeds, with zero fuzz tools/ the build script and its helpers docker/Dockerfile the pinned build environment .github/workflows/ the checks and the build

docs.title: On GitHub Actions
docs.text:
The build needs nothing but the repository.

Workflow When What it does check every push and pull request shell syntax, the version label, that the pins resolve, and a config check: feeds, patches, pins, defconfig and the seed checks, without compiling build by hand (Actions → build → Run workflow) or when a tag v<version> is pushed builds the image in the Docker environment, with a download cache and a compiler cache

The inputs of a manual run:

Input Default Meaning clean off rebuild every package opt_artifacts off also compile and verify the optional cw-opt feed artifacts off upload the images as a workflow artifact (public for a public repository) publish off create a GitHub release and update the project site

A job is limited to six hours by GitHub. A cold build takes roughly two hours; later builds are shorter because of the caches.

docs.title: Locally
docs.text:
You need a Linux machine (or a Linux VM) and Docker.

git clone --depth 1 --branch v25.12.5 https://github.com/openwrt/openwrt.git openwrt
docker build -t cleanwrt-builder docker/
docker run --rm \
  -v "$PWD/openwrt":/build -v "$PWD/cleanwrt-aw1000":/cleanwrt \
  cleanwrt-builder /cleanwrt/tools/cw-release-build.sh /build --clean

The sysupgrade image and a provenance bundle land in openwrt/bin/targets/qualcommax/ipq807x/.

Check first, compile later

CW_CHECK_ONLY=1 runs the feed, patch, pin, defconfig and seed checks and stops before compiling. Pass it with -e CW_CHECK_ONLY=1 to docker run. It takes a few minutes and catches almost every configuration mistake.

docs.title: What the build script guarantees
docs.text:
tools/cw-release-build.sh applies the overlay, the pinned feeds and the feed patches, then runs the mandatory post-defconfig fixups, and it fails rather than ship something stale:

  • the OpenWrt tree must be exactly at v25.12.5;
  • the version label in the seed and in the script must agree;
  • every feed and every local package must match its pinned commit;
  • a feed patch that no longer applies cleanly fails the build, because the upstream code changed;
  • every package the seed selects must survive make defconfig;
  • init scripts must be executable and use procd correctly;
  • the image must fit the flash layout (UBI_PEBS ... line) and the size gate;
  • the kernel modules repository the image points at must have the vermagic of the built kernel.

docs.title: Signing
docs.text:
Key Purpose How image signing (usign) signs every image tools/cw-sign-keys.sh --generate <tree> creates keys-release/. Never commit it. The build uses it when present. apk feed key signs the optional cw-opt feed created by the build tree on first build (private-key.pem). tools/cw-check-release-keys.sh proves a tree uses the key the devices trust.

On GitHub Actions these keys come from the repository secrets APK_PRIVATE_KEY, USIGN_KEY_BUILD and USIGN_KEY_BUILD_PUB. Without them the images are unsigned and the cw-opt feed stays disabled.

docs.title: Changing a patch or moving a pin
docs.text:
• Move a feed pin: change the commit after the ^ in feeds.conf.default, then make sure every patch in patches/feeds/ still applies (the check workflow does this).
  • Re-port a patch: apply it to the new upstream by hand, regenerate it with diff -u, and keep the header that says what it changes and why.

docs.title: 25.12.5-rc1
docs.text:
First release candidate.

  • OpenWrt 25.12.5 base for the Arcadyan AW1000 (qualcommax/ipq807x, kernel 6.12.94).
  • AWvoice: an ordinary desk phone on the RJ11 port makes and takes calls over the SIM, with caller id, call waiting, hold, three-way join (flash + 3), recall of a held call, call log, speed dial, call blocking, hotline and alarm calls.
  • 5G stack: QModem, vendor QMI dialer, 3ginfo-lite with a registration fix for data-only SIMs, SMS, TTL, vnStat.
  • Apex theme with dark and light mode and card-style status widgets.
  • Front-panel LED daemon (power, Wi-Fi, 5G type, signal, internet) with a night mode.
  • Proxy and VPN tools installed and disabled: Passwall, Passwall 2, HomeProxy, WireGuard, OpenVPN, Tailscale, Cloudflare Tunnel.
  • Opt-in apps installed and disabled: file sharing, DLNA, printer server, Syncthing, AdGuard Home, qBittorrent, Adblock, Disk Manager.
  • Built on GitHub Actions in a pinned Docker environment from pinned sources, with checksums and a provenance bundle.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Improvements are welcome: fixes, documentation, test reports and package suggestions.

docs.title: Reporting problems
docs.text:
See Repositories for which repository an issue belongs in.

Open an issue. Include:

  • the CleanWRT version (cat /etc/openwrt_release),
  • what you expected and what happened,
  • the relevant log lines (logread, or the output of cw-diag full).

Never post secrets

Do not paste passwords, Wi-Fi keys, tokens or full IMEI/IMSI/ICCID numbers.

docs.title: Changing the repository
docs.text:
main is protected. The rules:

  1. Every change is a pull request; nobody pushes to main directly.
  2. The checks must pass before a pull request can be merged.
  3. Pull requests are merged with squash merge, and the branch is deleted afterwards.
git clone https://github.com/Pr0Luci/cleanwrt-aw1000.git
cd cleanwrt-aw1000
git checkout -b my-change
# edit, then:
git commit -am "Short description of the change"
git push -u origin my-change

Then open a pull request on GitHub.

docs.title: Writing docs
docs.text:
The documentation is the docs/ folder, built with MkDocs Material. Every page has an Edit this page button that opens the right file on GitHub.

pip install mkdocs-material
mkdocs serve        # preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000

The package list page is generated from the build seed; do not edit it by hand.

docs.title: Rules for changes to the firmware
docs.text:
• Keep the overlay small. A new file in files/ ships on every router.
  • A new feed patch must apply with zero fuzz to the pinned commit. Say in its header what it changes and why.
  • Anything that adds a listening service must ship disabled.
  • Do not add translations or internal wording. Keep comments plain and short.
  • Do not commit keys. keys-release/ and private-key.pem are ignored for a reason.

docs.title: From the official repositories
docs.text:
The official OpenWrt 25.12.5 repositories are enabled on every router:

apk update
apk add <package>

Examples that are not part of the image: mwan3 and luci-app-mwan3 (multi-WAN), transmission-daemon (another download client), aria2, luci-app-acme (certificates).

Packages you add yourself stay unpinned and are yours to manage.

docs.title: The optional CleanWRT feed (cw-opt)
docs.text:
CleanWRT can publish its own signed apk feed for packages the official repositories do not carry, such as OpenClash. The feed is not active in the 25.12.5-rc1 image: the repository holds a disabled template, files/etc/apk/repositories.d/cw-opt.list.disabled, and the feed is switched on only when its index is published and its signing key exists.

How it is enabled (for the project, not for users):

  1. Build once so the tree creates its apk signing key.
  2. Copy the public half to files/etc/apk/keys/public-key.pem.
  3. Publish the index first. An image that carries a dead feed entry breaks apk update on every device.
  4. Rename the file to cw-opt.list and rebuild.

Until then, apk update talks to the official repositories only, and it works from the first boot.

docs.title: What is already baked in
docs.text: qBittorrent and AdGuard Home are part of the image, with the Qt6 stack that qBittorrent needs. They come from the project's vendored feed (feeds-src/cwfeed) and stay disabled until you enable them.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Only the Arcadyan AW1000, and only with the expanded flash layout. See MTD layout.
  • The first install from the stock firmware needs a serial console.
  • QModem is not free for commercial use. Its licence adds a non-commercial clause. See Licence and notices.
  • AWvoice is not for emergency calls. See the safety notes on the AWvoice page.
  • Images are unsigned unless the project's image-signing key is configured for the release.
  • The cw-opt package feed is not active yet.
  • The modem's own firmware is separate and is not provided by this project.

docs.title: Questions
docs.text:
Does OpenWrt run on the Arcadyan AW1000?

Yes. CleanWRT is OpenWrt 25.12.5 built for the AW1000 (qualcommax/ipq807x), with the 5G modem, Wi-Fi, the front-panel LEDs and the RJ11 phone port working. It needs the expanded flash layout, see the MTD layout page.

Can I use a normal phone on the AW1000's RJ11 port?

Yes, with AWvoice, which is part of CleanWRT: an ordinary analogue phone makes and takes calls over the SIM.

Does the AW1000 do VoLTE voice calls on OpenWrt?

Yes, with AWvoice. The 5G modem carries the call over VoLTE, so you need a SIM and an operator that provide VoLTE.

Why does the browser say the connection is not secure?

LuCI uses a self-signed certificate created on your router at first boot. The connection is encrypted, but no public authority signed the certificate. See Security.

I cannot log in after flashing.

The first login is over Ethernet with no password, at http://192.168.1.1. Connect a computer to a LAN port and set its address to 192.168.1.x if it does not get one. If it still fails, use failsafe mode.

Can I flash it on my router if it is not an AW1000?

No. Never flash an image built for another device. It can brick the router.

sysupgrade says the image is not valid.

Check the file name (arcadyan_aw1000), re-download the image and check its checksum. If you flash a community build that has no metadata, you would need -F; do not force an image you did not verify.

The 5G modem does not register.

Open Modem → QModem and Modem → 3gInfo-lite and check the SIM, the APN and the signal. See The 5G modem. A modem firmware upgrade is only a last resort.

The 5G and signal LEDs went dark.

The LED daemon cannot read the modem. Check that nothing holds the AT port open, and read logread -e cw-led. See Front-panel LEDs.

Wi-Fi works but 'Internet' says unreachable.

Open the connectivity check settings in System → LED Management. The LED only mirrors the probe. Test the real connection from a computer too.

Cloudflared shows a red error.

That is expected until you configure the tunnel token. See Remote access.

I ran apk upgrade and the overview cards look different.

The LuCI packages are pinned for a reason (see Updating and pinning). Flash the release again to get back to its state. A factory reset does not restore replaced packages.

Downloads are filling the router's flash.

Downloads default to the first USB drive. Plug a drive in before you start a download.

Can I use it commercially?

The project is free of charge. The bundled QModem component prohibits commercial use. Check its licence before you deploy this firmware in a business, an ISP or a paid service.

How do I go back to the stock firmware?

Restoring the stock firmware needs the stock image and a serial console. Keep a backup of the stock firmware before you flash.

What is the default IP address and login of CleanWRT on the AW1000?

The router answers at http://192.168.1.1 over Ethernet, with no root password at first. LuCI asks you to set one. Wi-Fi starts as CleanWRT-5G and CleanWRT-2.4G with the default key CleanWRT#40, so change it on the first login.

Do I need a serial cable to install OpenWrt on the AW1000?

For the first install from the stock firmware, yes: a 3.3 V USB-UART adapter and a TFTP server. If the router already runs OpenWrt, you can update with sysupgrade or from LuCI with no cable. See Installation.

Where do I download the AW1000 firmware, and how do I verify it?

On the GitHub Releases page of the project. Check the file with sha256sum -c sha256sums.cw --ignore-missing before you flash, and make sure the file name contains arcadyan_aw1000. See Releases.

How do I recover an AW1000 that will not boot?

If the router boots but you cannot reach it, use failsafe mode over Ethernet. If it is stuck at the bootloader, use the serial console to boot an initramfs image over TFTP and flash again. See Recovery.

docs.title: Still stuck?
docs.text:
1. Collect a diagnostic capture: cw-diag full (SIM identifiers, public IPs and Wi-Fi keys are redacted).
  2. Read the Recovery page.
  3. Open an issue on GitHub with the version, what you did, and the relevant log lines. Do not paste passwords or keys.

docs.title: First boot
docs.text: CleanWRT follows the stock OpenWrt first-login model.

docs.title: Defaults
docs.text:
Address 192.168.1.1 Hostname CleanWRT Root password none (set it on first login) Wi-Fi on, WPA2-PSK, networks CleanWRT-2.4G, CleanWRT-5G (and CleanWRT-6G on a 6 GHz radio) Default Wi-Fi key CleanWRT#40 Time zone UTC (set yours in LuCI) Admin UI LuCI over HTTPS (self-signed certificate) Opt-in apps installed, disabled

Change both on the first login

Anyone who knows the default Wi-Fi key can join your network, and with no root password anyone on the LAN can log in. Do the steps below before you connect the router to anything you do not trust.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Connect a computer to a LAN port with Ethernet. Do not use Wi-Fi for the first login.
  2. Open http://192.168.1.1. The browser is moved to HTTPS and shows a certificate warning. That is expected, see Security.
  3. LuCI asks you to set a root password. Set a strong one. It applies to LuCI and SSH.

  4. Change the Wi-Fi key: Network → Wireless, edit each interface, Wireless Security.

    uci set wireless.default_radio0.key='your-strong-key'
uci set wireless.default_radio1.key='your-strong-key'
uci commit wireless && wifi reload

  5. Set your time zone: System → System → General Settings.

  6. Open Modem and check that the 5G modem registered. See The 5G modem.

The root password is set under System → Administration:

Upgrades with keep settings never overwrite a key you have set yourself.

docs.title: Turning on an app
docs.text: Every opt-in app has the same single switch: open its LuCI page, tick Enable, press Save & Apply. Set any passwords the app needs before you enable it. See What is included.

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text:
CleanWRT supports one device: the Arcadyan AW1000 5G router (the Telstra variant).

No other device

Flashing this image on any other router can brick it. The partition table lives on the router, not in the image, and an image built for a different table is the classic way to destroy a router.

docs.title: Specification
docs.text:
SoC Qualcomm IPQ8072 (ipq807x), four cores Memory 1 GiB RAM, 1 GiB NAND flash 5G modem Quectel RG500Q-EA (separate firmware, see The 5G modem) Wi-Fi Qualcomm ath11k radios Ethernet Qualcomm NSS data plane Kernel Linux 6.12.94 Target qualcommax/ipq807x, board name arcadyan,aw1000 OpenWrt base 25.12.5

The official OpenWrt Table of Hardware page has further background on the device.

docs.title: Front panel
docs.text: The router has indicator LEDs for power, Wi-Fi, 5G, signal, internet and phone. CleanWRT drives the first five; see Front-panel LEDs. The phone LED belongs to AWvoice and is left alone by the LED app.

docs.title: The phone port
docs.text: The AW1000 has an RJ11 socket with a line-interface chip, for an ordinary analogue phone. AWvoice uses it to make and take calls over the SIM card. Mind the voltages on the contacts, and see the safety notes on that page.

docs.title: What you need to know before flashing
docs.text:
• The router must have the expanded flash layout. The stock layout is too small. See MTD layout.
  • The first install from the stock firmware needs a serial console. See the UART guide.
  • Keep a copy of the stock firmware settings if you may ever want to go back.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
What chip and memory does the Arcadyan AW1000 have?

A Qualcomm IPQ8072 with four cores, 1 GiB of RAM and 1 GiB of NAND flash. Wi-Fi comes from Qualcomm ath11k radios, and the Ethernet ports sit on the NSS data plane.

Which 5G modem is inside the Arcadyan AW1000?

A Quectel RG500Q-EA. Its firmware is separate from the router firmware, so flashing CleanWRT does not touch it. See The 5G modem.

Which AW1000 does CleanWRT run on?

The Arcadyan AW1000 in its Telstra variant, and nothing else. The image is built for board arcadyan,aw1000 on qualcommax/ipq807x, and an image for a different partition table can brick a router.

Does the Arcadyan AW1000 have a phone port?

Yes. It has an RJ11 socket with a line-interface chip. With AWvoice an ordinary analogue desk phone can make and take calls over the SIM card.

docs.title: IPv6 and proxies
docs.text: The 5G connection is dual-stack when your carrier offers IPv6. If you send traffic through Passwall 2, enable IPv6 TProxy in its forwarding settings. To use IPv4 only, set the modem's PDP type to IPv4 in Modem → QModem.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Read this page fully before you start

Supported hardware is the Arcadyan AW1000 only. Flashing the wrong image or flashing on the wrong flash layout can brick the router. Read MTD layout and Recovery before you flash.

There are two situations:

  1. The router already runs OpenWrt (stock OpenWrt 25.12.x or an earlier CleanWRT). Go to Already on OpenWrt.
  2. The router runs the stock (Telstra) firmware. The first OpenWrt install needs serial console (UART) access. Go to First install from stock.

docs.title: What you need for a first install
docs.text:
• A 3.3 V USB-UART adapter. Do not use 5 V logic. Plus a few wires.
  • A Phillips screwdriver to open the case, and a look at the UART guide to find the pads.
  • A TFTP server on your computer (atftpd, tftpd-hpa, or dnsmasq --enable-tftp) with a fixed IP in the router's LAN range (factory default 192.168.1.x).
  • Two files from a release (see Releases):
    • …-initramfs-uImage.itb, the boot-in-RAM image for the first install
    • …-squashfs-sysupgrade.bin, the permanent image
  • An Ethernet cable. The first login is over Ethernet.

docs.title: First install from stock firmware (UART + TFTP)
docs.text:
1. Open the case, connect the UART adapter (3.3 V!) and open a serial terminal at 115200 8N1 (screen /dev/ttyUSB0 115200, or PuTTY).
  2. Power the router on and interrupt U-Boot when the countdown appears (press a key).

  3. Tell U-Boot the router's IP and your TFTP server's IP:

    setenv ipaddr 192.168.1.1
setenv serverip 192.168.1.10   # your computer running TFTP

  4. Boot the initramfs image from RAM:

    tftpboot ${loadaddr} <initramfs-image-name>.itb
bootm ${loadaddr}

  5. The router boots a live OpenWrt from RAM. Flash the permanent image from this live system, over the network:

    # from your computer
scp *-squashfs-sysupgrade.bin root@192.168.1.1:/tmp/
# on the router
sysupgrade -v /tmp/*-squashfs-sysupgrade.bin

  6. The router reboots into the permanent firmware. Continue with First boot.

The no-UART shortcut

On very old stock firmware revisions a community "autoscript" method exists (flashing via a crafted USB update file, no UART). It is not maintained here, the older methods are reported to be patched on newer stock firmware, and a wrong image for your flash layout can brick the device. Prefer UART + TFTP.

docs.title: Already on OpenWrt (sysupgrade)
docs.text:
scp *-arcadyan_aw1000-squashfs-sysupgrade.bin root@192.168.1.1:/tmp/
ssh root@192.168.1.1 "sysupgrade -v /tmp/*-sysupgrade.bin"
  • Keep settings (the default): your configuration survives. This is fine between CleanWRT releases.
  • Clean install (sysupgrade -n): wipes the overlay. Use it when changing major versions, when the UI misbehaves, or when coming from a much older build. It also puts the default credentials back (see First boot).

You can also upload the image in LuCI, under System → Backup / Flash Firmware → Flash image….

Before flashing from OpenWrt, check the layout:

cat /proc/mtd

The rootfs partition must be at least 0x08000000 (128 MiB). Otherwise stop. See MTD layout.

docs.title: After flashing
docs.text:
• Open http://192.168.1.1 over Ethernet and follow First boot.
  • Check the version in the login banner or Status → Overview.
  • If something is wrong, go to Recovery.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
How do I install OpenWrt on the Arcadyan AW1000 for the first time?

From the stock firmware you need a 3.3 V USB-UART adapter and a TFTP server. Stop U-Boot on the serial console, boot the initramfs image from RAM over TFTP, then run sysupgrade from that live system to write the permanent image.

Can I install OpenWrt on the AW1000 without opening the case?

If the router already runs OpenWrt, yes: copy the sysupgrade image over and flash it, or use System → Backup / Flash Firmware in LuCI. From the stock firmware you need the serial console. A community no-UART method existed for very old stock firmware, but it is not maintained here and is reported to be patched on newer revisions.

Which file do I flash on the AW1000, initramfs or sysupgrade?

Both, in order, on a first install. The initramfs image only boots a live system from RAM and writes nothing. The sysupgrade image is the permanent one. Later updates need only the sysupgrade image.

Should I keep settings or use sysupgrade -n on the AW1000?

Keep settings between CleanWRT releases. Use sysupgrade -n (a clean install) when you change major versions, when you come from another firmware, or when the interface misbehaves. It also puts the default credentials back.

docs.title: Front-panel LEDs
docs.text:
CleanWRT replaces the stock LED Configuration page with LED Management (System → LED Management), backed by a small daemon, cw-led-daemon. The package is luci-app-cw-led.

The LEDs on this board are on/off only (no dimming).

docs.title: The status card
docs.text:
The top of the page shows the live state of the LEDs, refreshed every few seconds, so you can see what the panel shows without looking at the router.

DarkLightOn a phone

About the screenshots

The screenshots in this documentation were taken from a development preview of the interface (the same theme, pages and LED app as the firmware) running on a computer, with a simulated modem. Values such as the kernel, memory and storage differ on a real router.

docs.title: What each LED shows
docs.text:
LED Shows Power always on Wi-Fi on while any radio is up. In single interface mode it blinks with traffic on one interface. 5G 5G type only: solid blue = 5G standalone (SA), solid green = 5G non-standalone (NSA), off for anything else (4G, 3G, no service, unknown). There is no red on this LED. Signal green good, blue average, red poor; flashing red while the modem is connecting or the SIM has a fault; off when the service is unavailable. Internet on while the connectivity check says the uplink really reaches the internet.

The phone LED is not controlled by this app: it belongs to AWvoice. When AWvoice is running it is solid while the line is ready, blinks fast while a call rings and blinks slowly while the handset is off hook.

docs.title: How signal quality is decided
docs.text:
The signal LED uses RSRP (in dBm), with CSQ as a fallback when RSRP is unavailable. The limits are settings:

Excellent (green) Poor (red) Between (blue) RSRP at or above -95 at or below -110 in between CSQ at or above 20 at or below 9 in between

docs.title: How the internet LED is decided
docs.text:
Active connectivity probe (HTTP 204) is the default and the most accurate. The daemon asks a test address for an empty "204" answer; anything else (a captive portal page, a redirect, a timeout) means "no internet". It catches the case where the link is up but there is no real connectivity. Two other modes exist: Default-route interface is up (link state only) and Ping a host.

  • One good probe turns the LED on quickly. It takes two failed probes in a row to turn it off, so a single dropped probe does not flicker the LED.
  • It follows the routing table and is not bound to one network device, so it works behind a transparent proxy on the router.

docs.title: Night mode
docs.text:
Night mode switches chosen LEDs off between two times of day.

Setting Default Enabled off Window 22:30 to 06:00 (a window past midnight is supported) Keep on during night all five LEDs are on the list, so nothing is dimmed until you remove entries

Remove an LED from Keep on during night to switch it off inside the window.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
All settings are on the LED Management page and stored in /etc/config/cw-led.

Section Option Default Meaning General enabled on run the daemon General poll_interval 30 seconds between modem polls Modem port /dev/ttyUSB2 AT port. If it does not answer, the daemon tries ttyUSB3, ttyUSB1, ttyUSB0. Modem timeout 3 AT response timeout (s) Modem fail_threshold 3 failed polls in a row before 5G and signal LEDs go off Modem grace_max_ticks 2 polls to keep the last colour when a reply is cut short (0 = off) Internet mode http204 http204, interface or ping Internet probe_url http://cp.cloudflare.com/generate_204 test address, plain http:// so captive portals are detected

Restart the service after editing the file by hand:

/etc/init.d/cw-led restart

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Read the log

Every change of the 5G or signal colour is logged with the modem state: logread -e cw-led

Symptom Likely cause 5G and signal LEDs are off the modem is unreachable on the AT port. Check the port in the settings and that nothing else holds it open. LEDs flicker or go blank for a moment another program reads the same AT port. The default ttyUSB2 is chosen so QModem (on ttyUSB3) does not share it. Internet LED stays off though the internet works the probe address is blocked. Change Probe URL or switch to Default-route interface is up. Wi-Fi LED off with the radios up in single interface mode the LED follows one interface only. Use Auto.

If the daemon stops, the power and Wi-Fi LEDs return to their normal kernel triggers and the daemon-owned LEDs are turned off.

docs.title: Under the hood
docs.text: The daemon reads the modem directly over the AT port with plain shell, so no other app is needed. It writes the LED state through sysfs, only when something changes. The source is in the luci-app-cw-led repository.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
What do the front-panel LEDs of the Arcadyan AW1000 mean?

Power is always on. Wi-Fi is on while a radio is up. The 5G LED shows the 5G type: solid blue for standalone, solid green for non-standalone, off for anything else. Signal is green, blue or red for good, average or poor. Internet is on while a real connectivity check passes.

How do I turn off the AW1000 LEDs at night?

Enable night mode in System → LED Management. The default window is 22:30 to 06:00, and a window past midnight works. Remove an LED from the keep-on list to switch it off inside the window.

Why is the 5G LED on my AW1000 off?

The 5G LED lights only for 5G. It is off on 4G, 3G, with no service, or when the type is unknown. If the signal LED is off too, the daemon probably cannot read the modem on its AT port.

Why is the internet LED off when my internet works?

The LED mirrors a connectivity probe. If the probe address is blocked, it stays off. Change the probe URL in LED Management, or switch the check to the default-route mode.

docs.title: The 5G modem
docs.text: The AW1000 has a Quectel RG500Q-EA 5G modem. CleanWRT drives it with QModem and the vendor QMI dialer, so it dials and recovers on its own.

docs.title: What works out of the box
docs.text:
Feature Where Notes Modem control and status Modem → QModem auto-dial, auto-recovery, dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 when your carrier offers IPv6 Signal and network details Modem → 3gInfo-lite registration shows correctly on data-only SIMs (a CEREG-based fix) SMS Modem → SMS read and send; received SMS can be forwarded Carrier tethering-detection bypass (TTL) Modem → TTL on by default: forwarded packets get a fixed TTL of 64 Data usage Statistics → vnStat daily and monthly totals on the modem interface Wi-Fi regulatory domain automatic taken from the network's country code once the modem registers

About the TTL setting

The TTL rule exists so tethered traffic looks like traffic from the router itself. Whether that is allowed depends on your carrier's terms. You can change the value or turn it off in Modem → TTL.

docs.title: AWvoice and the modem
docs.text: AWvoice uses the modem for voice calls (VoLTE) and needs it in PCM slave mode. If you use the phone port, read that page before you change the modem's audio or IMS settings.

docs.title: IPv4 only
docs.text: To use IPv4 only, set the modem's PDP type to IPv4 in Modem → QModem. If you send traffic through Passwall 2, also enable IPv6 TProxy in its forwarding settings, otherwise devices can reach IPv6 sites directly, outside the proxy.

docs.title: AT ports
docs.text:
The modem exposes several serial ports. Two of them are for AT commands:

Port Used by /dev/ttyUSB2 the LED daemon (see Front-panel LEDs) /dev/ttyUSB3 QModem

Do not keep a port open

Two programs reading one AT port interleave their replies. Do not leave a terminal open on either port for a long time: a stuck session can blank the LEDs or stall QModem. Close the session when you are done.

docs.title: Modem firmware
docs.text: The modem's firmware is separate from the router firmware. Flashing CleanWRT does not change it. CleanWRT does not ship, host or redistribute Quectel firmware or tools, and the project has not performed the upgrade itself: it is the vendor's procedure and your risk.

docs.title: 1. Read the current version (safe, changes nothing)
docs.text:
Easiest is the QModem page, which shows the firmware revision. Over SSH:

( timeout 3 cat /dev/ttyUSB3 > /tmp/at.out & ); sleep 1; printf 'ATI\r' > /dev/ttyUSB3; sleep 2
tr -d '\r' < /tmp/at.out; rm -f /tmp/at.out

A reply looks like this:

ATI      ->  Quectel / RG500Q-EA / Revision: RG500QEAAAR13A01M4G
AT+QGMR  ->  RG500QEAAAR13A01M4G_01.200.01.200

docs.title: 2. When is an upgrade needed?
docs.text: Only when the modem misbehaves on your carrier (no registration, no 5G, unstable data) and the carrier or Quectel confirms that a newer firmware fixes it. Some units are reported to ship with a region-customised firmware that works poorly on other carriers; the revision string is what to quote when asking Quectel. If the modem works, leave it alone.

docs.title: 3. Where the firmware comes from
docs.text: Only from Quectel (or your supplier acting for Quectel): the package for your exact module variant and revision, with the vendor's release notes. Do not use packages from forums or other sites. A wrong or modified package can brick the modem.

docs.title: 4. The upgrade (vendor procedure)
docs.text:
Quectel's Linux flashing tool is QFirehose. It is not in the OpenWrt 25.12.5 package feeds and not in the CleanWRT feed; it comes with the vendor's Linux tools package. Follow the README of the version you receive, because the flags differ between versions. In outline:

  1. Read the version (step 1) and keep the output.
  2. Power the router from a stable supply and do not touch it during the flash.

  3. Stop what uses the modem ports:

    /etc/init.d/cw-led stop
/etc/init.d/qmodem_network stop
/etc/init.d/qmodem_monitor stop

  4. Run QFirehose against the unpacked vendor firmware directory, as its README says.

  5. Wait for the modem to re-enumerate, read the version again, then start the services again (or reboot).

docs.title: 5. Risk and recovery
docs.text:
• An interrupted or wrong flash can leave the modem unusable. A downgrade is not guaranteed to work: plan as if the upgrade is one-way.
  • The router itself is unaffected, so SSH and LuCI stay reachable over LAN and Wi-Fi.
  • If the modem does not come back, the vendor's tool and package are the recovery path. Contact Quectel with the revision string you saved.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Why does the 5G modem of my AW1000 not register?

Open Modem → QModem and Modem → 3gInfo-lite and check the SIM, the APN and the signal first. A modem firmware upgrade is only a last resort, and only when the carrier or Quectel confirms that a newer firmware fixes your problem.

How do I read and send SMS on the Arcadyan AW1000?

Use Modem → SMS in LuCI. You can read and send messages there, and received SMS can be forwarded.

What does the TTL setting do on the AW1000?

It gives forwarded packets a fixed TTL of 64 so tethered traffic looks like traffic from the router itself. It is on by default. Whether that is allowed depends on your carrier's terms, and you can change or switch it off in Modem → TTL.

How do I use IPv4 only on the AW1000 5G connection?

Set the modem's PDP type to IPv4 in Modem → QModem. If you send traffic through Passwall 2, also enable IPv6 TProxy in its forwarding settings so devices cannot reach IPv6 sites outside the proxy.

Which AT port do I use on the AW1000 modem?

The modem exposes two AT ports. The LED daemon uses /dev/ttyUSB2 and QModem uses /dev/ttyUSB3. Do not leave a terminal open on either one, because two programs reading one port interleave their replies.

Do I need to upgrade the modem firmware on my AW1000?

Only if the modem misbehaves on your carrier. If it works, leave it alone. The firmware is separate from CleanWRT, comes only from Quectel, and an interrupted or wrong flash can leave the modem unusable.

docs.title: MTD layout
docs.text:
Read this before the first flash

CleanWRT does not fit the stock flash layout of the AW1000. It needs the expanded layout. Flashing it on a stock layout can leave the router unbootable (UART + TFTP recovery needed).

docs.title: What actually has to fit
docs.text:
What must fit is the set of UBI volumes inside the rootfs MTD partition, not the size of the sysupgrade file.

A stock-layout AW1000 has a 100 MiB rootfs partition (0x06400000, which is 400 erase blocks of 256 KiB). UBI reserves part of it for itself:

Reserved by UBI Blocks layout volume 2 wear leveling and erase-block bookkeeping 2 bad-block reserve (20/1024 of the whole 1 GiB chip, whatever the partition size) 80

So 316 blocks (about 76 MiB) are left for volumes. The stock firmware's own UBI on that partition uses exactly 316 (kernel 24 + rootfs 177 + rootfs_data 115).

docs.title: What CleanWRT needs
docs.text:
The 25.12.5-rc1 image needs 498 blocks. That is more than the stock layout offers (316) and fits the expanded layout (2720 blocks on a router with a 701 MiB rootfs). The release build prints a line like this and fails if the image does not fit:

UBI_PEBS volumes need 498 PEBs; stock 100 MiB layout (316): does NOT fit; gate layout=expanded (capacity 2720)

A sysupgrade that cannot create the new volumes after removing the old ones can leave the router unbootable.

docs.title: Check your router
docs.text:
On a router running OpenWrt:

cat /proc/mtd
  • The rootfs partition must be at least 0x08000000 (128 MiB, 512 blocks).
  • On a stock layout that partition appears as rootfs_bak / rootfs1_bak instead. If you see that, do not flash this image.

Never flash an image built for another layout

The partition table lives on the router, not in the image. An image built for a different table can brick the router.

docs.title: If your router has the stock layout
docs.text:
CleanWRT does not convert the layout. Use a layout-conversion procedure from the OpenWrt community for this device first, and only then install CleanWRT. Make sure you can reach the serial console before you start; you will need it if anything goes wrong.

Next: Recovery. Read it before you flash.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
How do I check the flash layout of my Arcadyan AW1000?

Run cat /proc/mtd on a router that runs OpenWrt. The rootfs partition must be at least 0x08000000 (128 MiB). If it shows up as rootfs_bak instead, you have the stock layout, so do not flash this image.

Why does OpenWrt not fit on the stock AW1000 flash layout?

The stock rootfs partition leaves 316 erase blocks for UBI volumes, and the CleanWRT image needs 498. The build checks this and fails if the image does not fit the layout it targets.

Can I flash CleanWRT if my AW1000 has the stock layout?

No. CleanWRT does not convert the layout. Use a layout-conversion procedure from the OpenWrt community first, make sure you can reach the serial console, and only then install.

docs.title: Recovery and unbrick
docs.text:
Read this page before you flash. The AW1000 has a single NAND layout with no A/B fallback partition. A bad write to the kernel or rootfs partitions leaves you at the bootloader, and recovery needs the serial console.

Pick the situation that matches yours:

Situation Go to the router boots, but LuCI or SSH is unreachable or misconfigured Failsafe mode boot loop, the LEDs stop early, or a sysupgrade was interrupted Bootloader recovery the serial console shows nothing at all U-Boot is broken

docs.title: Failsafe mode
docs.text:
Use it when the router boots but you cannot reach it.

  1. Set your computer's network card to 192.168.1.x (for example 192.168.1.10) and connect to a LAN port with Ethernet.
  2. Power-cycle the router. When the boot LED starts blinking, press the reset button a few times; failsafe starts if a press is registered during boot.

  3. The router comes up at 192.168.1.1 with SSH and no root password.

    ssh root@192.168.1.1
mount_root          # mount the overlay so you can edit your config
firstboot && reboot # factory reset (destroys your configuration)
# or fix the specific file under /overlay/upper/... and then: reboot

Failsafe works only over Ethernet. It does not work over Wi-Fi or the 5G modem.

docs.title: Bootloader level recovery (U-Boot alive)
docs.text:
Symptoms: boot loop, the LED stops early, or you interrupted a sysupgrade.

  1. Connect the UART and interrupt U-Boot.
  2. Boot an initramfs image over TFTP (tftpboot then bootm, see Installation). Nothing is written to flash, so this works even with a corrupt rootfs.
  3. From the live RAM system, run sysupgrade -v with a full *-sysupgrade.bin.

docs.title: U-Boot itself is broken
docs.text: If the bootloader does not answer on the UART (no prompt, no countdown), recovery means reprogramming the NAND chip externally, with a programmer clipped onto the chip or after removing it. That is the real brick wall. It is why you should double-check the MTD layout and the image name before every flash.

docs.title: What sysupgrade keeps
docs.text:
Mode Result default (keep settings) /etc/config/* and the overlay survive: passwords, Wi-Fi keys and enabled services carry across releases sysupgrade -n clean slate: no root password, Wi-Fi back to the default key CleanWRT#40, every opt-in service back to disabled

Upgrades do not re-run first-boot scripts

On a keep-settings upgrade, fixes to defaults apply only to settings that are still at their default. When a release note mentions a default-credential fix, do a sysupgrade -n or rotate the affected credentials by hand.

docs.title: Packages replaced by apk upgrade
docs.text: A factory reset does not restore packages that apk upgrade replaced. To get back to the state of a release, flash that release again. See Updating and pinning.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
How do I unbrick an Arcadyan AW1000?

If U-Boot still answers on the serial console, interrupt it, boot an initramfs image over TFTP (nothing is written to flash), then run sysupgrade with a full image from that live system. If U-Boot itself is dead, the NAND has to be reprogrammed with an external programmer.

How do I enter failsafe mode on the AW1000?

Connect a computer over Ethernet and set it to 192.168.1.x, power-cycle the router, and press the reset button a few times once the boot LED starts blinking. The router then comes up at 192.168.1.1 over SSH with no root password. Failsafe does not work over Wi-Fi or the 5G modem.

What happens if a sysupgrade is interrupted on the AW1000?

You may end up in a boot loop or at the bootloader. The AW1000 has a single NAND layout with no A/B fallback partition, so recovery goes through the serial console and an initramfs image.

Does a factory reset undo an apk upgrade?

No. A factory reset does not restore packages that apk upgrade replaced. Flash the release image again to get back to the state of that release.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text: Images are published on the project's GitHub Releases page. Every release is built by the build workflow in the repository, from the sources pinned in the release tag.

docs.title: Versions
docs.text:
A version looks like 25.12.5-rc1: the OpenWrt base (25.12.5) and the stage.

Stage Meaning -rc1, -rc2 ... release candidates. They are the testing series. -rc1.1 ... a fix after the candidate was published no suffix (25.12.5) a stable release

docs.title: What a release contains
docs.text: File What it is cleanwrt-<version>-qualcommax-ipq807x-arcadyan_aw1000-squashfs-sysupgrade.bin the permanent image, installed with sysupgrade …-initramfs-uImage.itb a boot-in-RAM image, used for the very first install from the stock firmware …-squashfs-factory.ubi the raw UBI image *.manifest every package in the image with its version profiles.json machine-readable image description (also used by the LuCI update check) sha256sums, sha256sums.cw checksums of the images and of the provenance files provenance.tar.gz the full build .config, the seed, the pinned feed list, the local package pins and the exact source commits

docs.title: Verify before you flash
docs.text:
Always check the checksum. A corrupted image is the most common cause of a bad flash.

Linux / macOSWindows (PowerShell) 
sha256sum -c sha256sums.cw --ignore-missing

Get-FileHash .\cleanwrt-*-sysupgrade.bin -Algorithm SHA256
# compare with the matching line in sha256sums.cw

Check the model too

The filename must contain arcadyan_aw1000. Never flash an image built for another device or another flash layout.

docs.title: Update notice in LuCI
docs.text: The Status → Overview page can tell you when a newer CleanWRT is published. It reads a small file on the project site, so it needs internet access. You can switch it off any time with Stop showing upgrade alerts. The check never installs anything.

docs.title: Reproducing a release
docs.text: The release tag, configs/arcadyan_aw1000.seed, feeds.conf.default, configs/local-packages.pin and patches/ are the complete input. See Build from source.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Where can I download CleanWRT for the Arcadyan AW1000?

From the project's GitHub Releases page. Each release has the sysupgrade image, the initramfs image for a first install, a package manifest, checksums and a provenance bundle.

How do I check the checksum of the image before flashing?

On Linux or macOS run sha256sum -c sha256sums.cw --ignore-missing in the folder with the files. On Windows use Get-FileHash in PowerShell and compare the value with the matching line. A corrupted image is the most common cause of a bad flash.

What does rc1 mean in a CleanWRT version?

It is a release candidate: the testing series before a stable release. In 25.12.5-rc1, 25.12.5 is the OpenWrt base and rc1 is the first candidate. A suffix such as rc1.1 is a fix published after the candidate.

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text:
CleanWRT is built from a few small repositories, all on GitHub under Pr0Luci. The firmware repository pins the others to an exact commit.

Repository What it is Documentation cleanwrt-aw1000 the firmware: build configuration, patches, rootfs overlay, workflows and this documentation Build from source, Contributing openwrt-aw1000-voice-awvoice AWvoice: the kernel module, the phone daemon and the LuCI page for the RJ11 port AWvoice luci-app-cw-led the front-panel LED daemon and its LuCI page Front-panel LEDs luci-theme-apex the Apex LuCI theme The Apex theme

docs.title: How they fit together
docs.text:
cleanwrt-aw1000  (feeds.conf.default, configs/local-packages.pin, patches/)
   ├── pins  luci-app-cw-led      → LED daemon and page
   ├── pins  luci-theme-apex      → default theme
   ├── pins  AWvoice              → phone port
   └── pins  OpenWrt, LuCI, QModem, Passwall, 3ginfo-lite, ... (upstream feeds)

A change in one of the smaller repositories reaches the firmware only when the firmware repository moves its pin to the new commit. That is a pull request of its own, so every release is built from commits you can read.

docs.title: Where to report things
docs.text:
• A problem with the firmware, a package or these docs: an issue in cleanwrt-aw1000.
  • A problem that is clearly inside one of the other parts: an issue in that repository.
  • A mistake on a docs page: Edit this page (the pencil at the top of every page) opens it on GitHub, and a pull request fixes it.

docs.title: The Apex theme
docs.text: Apex is the default LuCI theme in CleanWRT. It is a dense, technical interface that stays readable on a phone. The source is in the luci-theme-apex repository.

docs.title: What it looks like
docs.text:
• Dark by default, with an automatic light mode that follows your system, and a toggle in the top bar to force either one (your choice is remembered in the browser).
  • A sidebar for navigation and a drawer on small screens (a 390 px phone is a first-class target).
  • A teal accent colour and monospace type for technical values.
  • A dedicated login page, which also introduces AWvoice.
  • Card-style status widgets on Status → Overview for system, modem, memory and storage, instead of long tables.

docs.title: Screenshots
docs.text:
DarkLightPhone

The login page, dark and light:

Dark Light

About the screenshots

The screenshots in this documentation were taken from a development preview of the interface (the same theme, pages and LED app as the firmware) running on a computer, with a simulated modem. Values such as the kernel, memory and storage differ on a real router.

docs.title: Switching themes
docs.text:
Apex is selected on the first boot. To change it later:

System → System → Language and Style → Design

The stock Bootstrap theme stays installed as a fallback. Pages that use the card widgets fall back to the normal tables when another theme is active, so nothing is lost.

docs.title: Fonts
docs.text: The login page uses two self-hosted fonts, Inter and JetBrains Mono, licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. No font is loaded from an outside server.

docs.title: Notes for developers
docs.text:
The other parts of CleanWRT are on the Repositories page.

The theme is an ordinary LuCI ucode theme: header.ut, footer.ut and the login page sysauth.ut under ucode/template/themes/apex/, a stylesheet with design tokens (--ax-* custom properties) and a small script for the sidebar. The status widgets are produced by patches to the pinned LuCI and QModem feeds (patches/feeds/), and only render while Apex is the active theme.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Does CleanWRT have a dark mode?

Yes. The Apex theme is dark by default, switches to a light mode that follows your system, and has a toggle in the top bar to force either one. Your choice is remembered in the browser.

Does the Apex theme work on a phone?

Yes. A sidebar becomes a drawer on small screens, and a 390 px wide phone is a first-class target.

How do I switch back to the default OpenWrt theme?

Go to System → System → Language and Style → Design. The stock Bootstrap theme stays installed as a fallback, and pages with card widgets fall back to normal tables when another theme is active.

docs.title: UART guide
docs.text: The serial console (UART) is how you reach the bootloader. It is required for the first install from the stock firmware, and it is the universal recovery path as long as the bootloader is intact.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text: Item Notes USB-UART adapter 3.3 V logic only. A 5 V adapter can damage the board. Three jumper wires TX, RX and GND. Do not connect the adapter's power pin. Phillips screwdriver to open the case Terminal program screen, minicom, PuTTY or similar

docs.title: Connection settings
docs.text: Setting Value Speed 115200 baud Data / parity / stop 8N1 Flow control none

docs.title: Wiring
docs.text:
Locate the UART pads on the board. They are marked for TX, RX and GND.

  • Router TX to adapter RX
  • Router RX to adapter TX
  • Router GND to adapter GND

Cross the data lines: transmit goes to receive. If you see nothing, swap TX and RX before you suspect anything else.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
# Linux
screen /dev/ttyUSB0 115200
# macOS
screen /dev/tty.usbserial-XXXX 115200

Power the router on. You should see the boot messages. To stop the boot at the bootloader, press a key when the countdown appears. You are now at the U-Boot prompt, and the installation and recovery steps can continue from there.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Disconnect the adapter's power wire; the router must power itself.
  • Keep the serial session open while you flash; it shows exactly what failed if something does.
  • Close the terminal when you are done. A stuck terminal on the modem's AT port (not the board UART) is a different matter, see The 5G modem.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
What UART settings does the Arcadyan AW1000 use?

115200 baud, 8N1, no flow control, at 3.3 V logic. Connect router TX to adapter RX, router RX to adapter TX and ground to ground, and leave the adapter's power pin unconnected.

Can I use a 5 V serial adapter on the AW1000?

No. Use 3.3 V logic only. A 5 V adapter can damage the board.

I see nothing on the AW1000 serial console. What should I check?

Swap the TX and RX wires first, since the data lines must cross. Then check that the grounds are joined, that the speed is 115200, and that you open the terminal before you power the router on.

How do I stop U-Boot on the AW1000?

Power the router on with the serial terminal open and press a key when the countdown appears. You are then at the U-Boot prompt, ready for the installation or recovery steps.

docs.title: Firmware updates
docs.text: Install a new release with sysupgrade (see Installation). Keep settings between CleanWRT releases; use a clean install (-n) when changing major versions or when a release note asks for it.

docs.title: What is pinned, and why
docs.text:
An on-device apk upgrade once replaced the LuCI pages with the upstream builds and silently dropped the project's patches (the overview cards went back to plain tables). To prevent that, the following are pinned to the versions of the release:

Pinned Because every package from the LuCI feed the patched pages must never be replaced by a stock build base-files its files in /rom are read-only the kernel and every kmod-* they are tied to the running kernel; a kernel change is always a flash

They change only with the next firmware release.

Every other package is unpinned. apk update && apk upgrade delivers upstream security fixes (for example openssl, mbedtls, ca-bundle, uhttpd).

Upgrading packages restarts services

Upgrading packages restarts the affected services (network, Wi-Fi, web server) for a moment.

docs.title: If a package upgrade breaks something
docs.text: Recovery from a failed package upgrade is flashing the release again. A factory reset does not restore packages that were replaced.

docs.title: Pins are renewed after every flash
docs.text: The pin list is generated from the installed package database on the first boot after a flash, including a keep-settings sysupgrade. The pins therefore always match the running image, and an old pin can never demand a downgrade.

docs.title: Source pins in the repository
docs.text: For builders: every feed is pinned to a commit in feeds.conf.default, and the packages that are not feeds are pinned in configs/local-packages.pin. The build fails if a checkout does not match its pin. See Build from source.

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text: What Where Data usage on metered 5G Statistics → vnStat: daily and monthly totals on the modem interface (already tracked) Live bandwidth per host Tools → Bandwidth Monitor Signal and network details Modem → 3gInfo-lite System logs Status → System Log (or logread over SSH)

docs.title: Ad blocking
docs.text: Adblock is installed but off by default. Open Services → Adblock, tick Enabled, pick a blocklist and press Save & Restart (not only Save & Apply). Use Adblock or AdGuard Home, not both.

docs.title: Watchcat
docs.text: Tools → Watchcat is installed but has no rule, so it does nothing until you add one. The 5G modem already re-dials on its own, so add a rule only if you want a whole-router or an interface watchdog.

docs.title: Quality of service
docs.text: Network → SQM QoS is installed and inert. Set your interface and your real bandwidth to fight bufferbloat. BBR congestion control is already on, which suits cellular links.

docs.title: Command line diagnostics
docs.text:
cw-diag collects a redacted diagnostic capture:

cw-diag <modem|qmi-rx|nss|wifi|bridge|sysup|full>

The output goes to /var/log/cw-diag-<subsystem>-<time>.log. SIM identifiers, public IPs and Wi-Fi keys are redacted. Also installed: htop, mtr, iperf3, ethtool, usbutils.

docs.title: Multi-WAN failover
docs.text:
Add a second internet connection and let the router switch to it if 5G drops or hits a cap.

mwan3 is not in the image

The 5G modem already reconnects by itself, so mwan3 is only needed to switch to a different connection. Install it when you need it:

apk add mwan3 luci-app-mwan3

docs.title: 1. Add the backup connection
docs.text:
Backup How Phone USB tether plug the phone in and turn on USB tethering; it appears as a network device (the rndis / ipheth driver loads automatically) USB modem or USB Ethernet adapter plug it in; usb-modeswitch turns dongles into modem mode

Add it under Network → Interfaces (DHCP).

docs.title: 2. Enable mwan3
docs.text:
/etc/init.d/mwan3 enable && /etc/init.d/mwan3 start

Configure members and policies in Network → Load Balancing. Point the primary at the modem interface (4_1) and the backup at your second connection.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Can the Arcadyan AW1000 fail over to another connection when 5G drops?

Yes, with mwan3. Add a phone USB tether, a USB modem or a USB Ethernet adapter as a second interface, then set the 5G modem as the primary member and the other as the backup.

Is mwan3 included in CleanWRT?

No. The 5G modem already reconnects by itself, so mwan3 is only needed to switch to a different connection. Install it with apk add mwan3 luci-app-mwan3.

docs.title: Remote access
docs.text:
5G gives you a CGNAT address, so port forwarding does not work. To reach the router or your LAN from outside, pick one of these. All of them ship disabled; enable only what you use.

Set a root password first

See Security. A tunnel to a router with no password is an open door.

docs.title: Tailscale
docs.text:
A mesh VPN, and the easiest option.

/etc/init.d/tailscale enable && /etc/init.d/tailscale start
tailscale up        # prints a login URL; open it to authenticate

The LuCI page is Services → Tailscale.

docs.title: Cloudflare Tunnel
docs.text:
Exposes a service through your Cloudflare account, with no public IP needed.

Services → Cloudflare Zero Trust Tunnel → Configuration: paste your tunnel token and enable.

A red cloudflared error is normal until you configure it

Until you set it up on the Configuration tab, the Tunnels and Log tabs show a red cloudflared error (config.yml was empty or no origin certificate). That is expected for an unconfigured tunnel, not a fault. Configure the token first.

docs.title: WireGuard
docs.text: You can also run your own WireGuard server on the router. See VPN and proxies.

docs.title: Which one?
docs.text: You want Use to reach the whole LAN from your devices with little setup Tailscale to publish one web service under your own domain Cloudflare Tunnel a classic VPN you control end to end (needs a public endpoint somewhere) WireGuard

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
How can I reach my router behind 5G CGNAT?

5G gives you a carrier-grade NAT address, so port forwarding does not work. Use Tailscale, a Cloudflare Tunnel or a WireGuard server you run yourself. All of them ship disabled.

Should I use Tailscale or Cloudflare Tunnel on the AW1000?

Tailscale is the easiest way to reach the whole LAN from your own devices. A Cloudflare Tunnel is better for publishing one web service under your own domain.

Why does cloudflared show a red error?

That is expected until you configure the tunnel token on the Configuration tab. It is not a fault.

docs.title: Defaults
docs.text:
CleanWRT starts the way stock OpenWrt does:

  • No root password at first. The first login happens over Ethernet, and LuCI asks you to set one.
  • Wi-Fi is on, WPA2-PSK, with the default key CleanWRT#40. Change it on the first login.
  • Every opt-in service is disabled. Nothing listens on your network until you enable it.
  • LuCI is served over HTTPS; plain HTTP only redirects to it.

See First boot for the steps.

Before you expose the router remotely

Set your root password first. Otherwise a tunnel publishes an admin interface with no password to the internet.

docs.title: Why the browser says "Not secure"
docs.text:
The admin UI uses a self-signed TLS certificate, generated on your router at first boot. Every router gets a different one and no public authority signed it, so browsers warn exactly as they do on stock OpenWrt. The connection is still encrypted. Click Advanced → Proceed.

If you own a domain, you can get a trusted certificate:

apk add acme-common luci-app-acme

Then issue a Let's Encrypt certificate with a DNS challenge (it works behind CGNAT).

docs.title: Changing the password and the Wi-Fi key later
docs.text:
• Root password: System → Administration, or passwd over SSH.
  • Wi-Fi key: Network → Wireless, edit the interface, Wireless Security.

No re-flash is needed.

docs.title: Keeping services private
docs.text: Service Reach Advice File sharing (SMB) LAN guest access is off; create users first qBittorrent web UI (:8080) LAN the first start prints a temporary password to the log; set your own Syncthing GUI (:8384) LAN set a GUI user and password before pairing AdGuard Home (:3000 wizard) LAN choose a dashboard port other than 80/443 miniDLNA (:8200) LAN only no login; do not expose it

docs.title: Reporting a problem
docs.text: For a security problem, please open a private report from the repository's Security tab (Report a vulnerability) if it is enabled, or open an issue that does not include exploit details and ask for a private channel.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Why does my browser say the OpenWrt router connection is not secure?

LuCI uses a self-signed certificate that your router creates at first boot. The connection is still encrypted, but no public authority signed the certificate. Click Advanced → Proceed, or install a trusted certificate with ACME if you own a domain.

What are the default passwords on CleanWRT?

There is no root password at first. The first login happens over Ethernet and LuCI asks you to set one. Wi-Fi is WPA2-PSK with the default key CleanWRT#40. Change both on the first login.

How do I get a trusted HTTPS certificate on the router?

Install acme-common and luci-app-acme, then issue a Let's Encrypt certificate with a DNS challenge. That works behind CGNAT because it needs no inbound connection.

docs.title: USB storage and NAS
docs.text: Plug in a USB drive and it auto-mounts under /mnt (ext4, FAT, exFAT and NTFS). Manage mounts in System → Mount Points.

docs.title: Prepare a drive in the browser
docs.text:
Services → Disk Manager creates partition tables (GPT or MBR), partitions and formats (ext4, FAT32, exFAT, NTFS, btrfs), and shows disk health (SMART, including USB-NVMe enclosures).

Mounts made in Disk Manager are live only

Set the boot-time mount in System → Mount Points afterwards so the drive is there after every reboot. The smartd daemon ships disabled; the UI only uses the smartctl command.

docs.title: NAS services (all opt-in)
docs.text:
Everything below ships installed but disabled and is pointed at the USB drive. Nothing listens on the LAN until you enable it. Set credentials before you enable each service.

Service Where Notes Network file share (SMB) Network → Filesystem Share serves all of /mnt as \\192.168.1.1\USB; guest access is off Torrents (qBittorrent) Services → qBittorrent web UI on :8080; downloads go to /mnt/download Folder sync (Syncthing) Services → Syncthing web UI on :8384 Media server (miniDLNA) Services → miniDLNA DLNA on the LAN only, port 8200 Printer share (p910nd) Services → p910nd raw port 9100 and mDNS Web file manager Tools → File Manager browse, edit, upload, delete, hex editor Drive spin-down Tools → HDD Idle for USB hard disks

More download clients are available from the official repositories:

apk add transmission-daemon transmission-web luci-app-transmission
apk add aria2 luci-app-aria2

Plug a drive in before you download

Downloads default to the first USB drive (/mnt/sda1). With no drive attached they would fill the router's small internal flash. Do not start downloads without a drive.

docs.title: Streaming to a TV or phone (DLNA)
docs.text:
1. Plug in a drive with media.
  2. Enable Services → miniDLNA; it scans /mnt.
  3. Smart TVs (Samsung, LG, Sony), VLC, Kodi, phone apps and a PS4/Xbox see the server on the LAN.

For a very large library, point the database directory at the drive (miniDLNA → Advanced), so it does not re-scan on every reboot.

PlayStation 5

The PS5 has no built-in DLNA player. Use an app such as Plex on it.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Can I use a USB drive as a NAS on the Arcadyan AW1000?

Yes. A drive auto-mounts under /mnt (ext4, FAT, exFAT and NTFS), and you can share it with SMB, DLNA, Syncthing and qBittorrent. All of these ship installed but disabled, so set credentials before you enable them.

Can the AW1000 stream media to a smart TV?

Yes. Enable miniDLNA with a drive of media attached. Smart TVs, VLC, Kodi and phone apps on the LAN will see the server. A PlayStation 5 has no built-in DLNA player, so use an app such as Plex there.

Why should I plug a drive in before downloading?

Downloads default to the first USB drive. With no drive attached they would fill the router's small internal flash.

docs.title: VPN and proxies
docs.text: All of these ship installed and disabled. They need your servers, keys or configuration.

docs.title: WireGuard
docs.text:
WireGuard is fully installed (kernel module, wg tools and LuCI protocol support) but has no interfaces configured. An empty Status page is normal until you create one.

Create a tunnel: Network → Interfaces → Add new interface, name it (for example wg0), protocol WireGuard VPN, Create interface. In the interface's Configuration tab set the private key and the peers (a peer is an endpoint plus allowed IPs).

Command line alternative:

wg genkey | tee privatekey | wg pubkey > publickey

then configure with wg set.

docs.title: OpenVPN
docs.text: VPN → OpenVPN. The service needs your .ovpn configuration, so it ships disabled. Enable it per configuration.

docs.title: Proxies and bypass tools
docs.text:
App Where Cores Passwall 2 Services → PassWall 2 Xray, Sing-box, Hysteria and more Passwall Services → PassWall the same cores HomeProxy Services → HomeProxy sing-box

Add a node (server), pick the matching core, set the routing mode and enable. dnsmasq-full and chinadns-ng are already wired in.

Use one proxy suite at a time

Running more than one proxy suite on the same router makes firewall and DNS rules fight. Enable the one you want.

IPv6: if you send traffic through Passwall 2, enable IPv6 TProxy in its forwarding settings. Passwall 1 hides IPv6 answers for proxied names by default.

docs.title: Common questions
docs.text:
Does CleanWRT include WireGuard and OpenVPN?

Yes. WireGuard is fully installed with no interfaces configured, and OpenVPN needs your own .ovpn configuration. Both ship disabled.

Can I run Passwall and HomeProxy at the same time?

It is better not to. Several proxy suites on one router make firewall and DNS rules fight, so enable the one you want.

Why do I need IPv6 TProxy in Passwall 2?

Without it, devices can reach IPv6 sites directly, outside the proxy. Enable it in the forwarding settings when you proxy traffic through Passwall 2.

docs.title: Apps with their own web interface
docs.text: Some apps are configured in their own dashboard, opened in the browser, and not inside LuCI. The three below are installed with the firmware. The examples assume the router is at 192.168.1.1.

docs.title: Start and stop an app
docs.text:
Every app has an Enable box on its LuCI page (Services → the app's name). Tick it and press Save & Apply to start; untick it and press Save & Apply to stop. One switch, the same everywhere.

Advanced: System → Startup lists services with Start and Stop buttons. They act only for the current session. The Enable box is what decides whether the app runs after a reboot.

docs.title: Syncthing: folder sync
docs.text:
Keeps folders in step between your phone, your PC and a drive on the router.

  1. Services → Syncthing, tick Enable, Save & Apply.
  2. Open the dashboard: http://192.168.1.1:8384.
  3. First thing to do: Actions → Settings → GUI, set a user name and password. Until then anyone on your network can open the dashboard.
  4. Add your other devices (Add Remote Device) and choose the folders to share.

To keep the dashboard private to the router itself, set the Dashboard address on the LuCI page to http://127.0.0.1:8384.

docs.title: AdGuard Home: DNS filtering
docs.text:
Blocks ads and trackers for every device and shows what each device looks up.

  1. Services → AdGuard Home, tick Enable, Save & Apply.
  2. The first time, the setup wizard is at http://192.168.1.1:3000.
  3. In the wizard choose a dashboard port other than 80 or 443 (LuCI uses those) and a DNS port other than 53, unless you move the router's own DNS (dnsmasq).
  4. Finish the wizard and open the dashboard at the address you chose.

Adblock does a similar job. Use one of them, not both.

docs.title: qBittorrent: download client
docs.text:
Downloads to a USB drive attached to the router, controlled from a web page.

  1. Services → qBittorrent, tick Enable, Save & Apply.
  2. Open http://192.168.1.1:8080.
  3. The user is admin. There is no shared default password: until you set your own, qBittorrent makes a temporary one every time it starts and prints it to the log. Read it with logread -e qbittorrent (System → Logs).
  4. Set your own: Tools → Options → Web UI → Authentication.

The default download folder is on the USB drive (/mnt); attach and mount it first.
